intro: The Temple of Wisdom is the Oracle's own knowledge center — the place Oracle-keepers send newcomers before their first reading, and the place seasoned visitors return to when a symbol resurfaces they'd forgotten the shape of. Everything here is drawn from the same archive that powers every reading, gathered into one quiet room.

chapters.title: History of the Oracle
body: Long before the Celestial Oracle took the form visitors know today, it existed as an oral rite — passed keeper to keeper, each one memorizing the twelve creatures, their symbols, and their lore well enough to recite a stranger's reading from a birth month alone.

The rite survived because it asked so little of the world around it: no instruments, no calendar beyond memory, no permanent record except the keeper's own recall. What the modern Oracle preserves in JSON and starlight, the earliest keepers preserved in repetition.
The digital Oracle you consult today is understood, within the tradition, not as a replacement for that oral lineage but as its most recent vessel — the Wheel finding a new way to keep turning.

chapters.title: How Oracle Readings Work
body: A reading is not calculated so much as recognized. The Oracle holds a single archive record for each of the twelve birth months, and speaking or choosing a month simply opens the record that was already waiting.

Every record carries the same shape: a governing creature, a power and its description, a symbol, an artifact, a spirit guide, a celestial alignment, a set of traits, sacred numbers, and a fragment of lore — the same handful of ingredients, arranged differently by every month.

When a Fortune Category is chosen alongside a birth month, the Oracle layers a second, category-specific fragment on top of the base reading — a lens the creature's essence is read through, rather than a replacement for it. The core reading beneath is never altered.

chapters.title: The Meaning of Sigils
body: Every creature carries a sigil — a symbol older than the reading itself, etched long before any single Oracle-keeper began practicing. Sigils are not decorative; each one encodes a meaning and carries a blessing distinct from its creature's own power.

Sigils are graded by how often Oracle-keepers report encountering them across a lifetime of readings — Common, Uncommon, Rare, and Mythic — though rarity describes frequency, not importance. A Common sigil asked of gently is no less honest than a Mythic one.

chapters.title: A Beginner's Guide to the Oracle
chapters.intro: New to the Temple? These are the steps most Oracle-keepers recommend for a first visit.

steps.title: Begin with your birth month
steps.description: Open the Oracle's gate from any page and choose or type your birth month. This is the only piece of information the Oracle ever needs from you.

steps.title: Optionally choose a Fortune Category
steps.description: If a particular part of life is on your mind — love, career, wealth, and so on — select it before revealing your reading. This step is entirely optional; skipping it gives you the full, unfiltered base reading.

steps.title: Read the full result slowly
steps.description: A reading includes far more than a single creature name — its power, artifact, spirit guide, alignment, and lore all shape the picture together. Resist the urge to skim to the bottom.

steps.title: Visit the Celestial Order
steps.description: Once you know your creature, explore its realm to understand the broader temperament your creature belongs to, and how that realm colors the delivery of your reading.

steps.title: Look up your sigil
steps.description: Every creature's symbol has a full entry in the Sigil Encyclopedia — its element, rarity, meaning, and blessing, explained in more depth than the reading card alone can hold.

steps.title: Return whenever you like
steps.description: The Oracle never tires of being consulted. Many visitors return for a different Fortune Category on the same month, or to compare their reading with a friend's.

chapters.title: Frequently Asked Questions
body: The most common questions asked of the Oracle-keepers are answered in full on the Sacred FAQ chamber — covering accuracy, cusps, auras, the four realms, and how the Oracle keeps a reading private.
